description: Her link: the one connection every device of the owner's keeps, to the server (today the site), and on the same 现场's LAN also directly to the PC her mind is on. Her state and every decision stay where her mind is; another end sends what it hears and sees up, and plays what comes down. Ends synthesize her voice themselves: her mind sends text and performance, never audio. Text frames only: each is canonical JSON with v, the frame format version (encoding). Protocol 2 is the only one spoken: an end that says hello in another is closed with unsupported_protocol (history says what protocol 1 was). Whether her log, her lease and the lent chats flow on a link is the welcome's sync, not a protocol number.

history.1: Protocol 1 (2026-10 to 2026-11-05): the site as her host and a native app as a child, the frames above without the families, and an envelope without v. Retired by the owner on 2026-11-05 with no fallback: every end speaks protocol 2, and the sync families are switched by welcome.sync.

auth.description: The device token the site owner made under Agent settings, devices. It is checked before the upgrade, without X-Sync-Clock. A refusal is a plain HTTP answer {error, code} and no upgrade. While she is moving (her host lease is frozen) the upgrade is refused with host_frozen; while she lives on another end, with host_moved and host: {kind, name}, the end she lives on (kind app and the device's name), or null when the site does not know. A plain GET of the path answers the same refusal, for a child that cannot read a refused upgrade.

timing.description: Each end pings every heartbeatMs and answers a ping with a pong. Nothing heard from the other end for missedHeartbeats heartbeats means the link is gone. A child reconnects with exponential backoff from reconnectInitialMs to reconnectMaxMs, and at once when the network comes back or the machine wakes. touchAppraiseMs is how long the host takes at most to answer touch.appraise. actPickupMs is how long an act.request waits for the child to start it or refuse it; actMaxRunMs is the longest one run it asks for may take on the child, which stops it then, and the host, a minute after that, counts it timed out. callAcceptMs is how long a long call (calls) waits for call.accepted; callDeadlineMaxMs is the longest a call that is not long may give from its ask to its deadlineAt (on the host's clock), longCallMaxMs that of a long one; the time it waits for the owner counts within it, and a receiver holds an ask to it from when it takes it. ownerConfirmMaxMs is how long a call waits for the owner to answer on the device before it ends declined. blobKeepMs is how long the host keeps a call's blob (transports.blobs) before it deletes it. deputyMaxMs is the longest a lease.deputy may run, from its issue to its end (the log rules' DEPUTY_MAX_MICROS): past a day her memory is no longer settled on the end thinking alone, and its last backup is older than what she wrote there.

limits.description: maxItems on a frame caps its arrays; a frame over any limit is refused with too_large or too_many. glanceChars caps input.glance's summary and each of its facts together: a child cuts a longer one before it sends it and a host cuts what still is, never refusing the frame for it. logPageBatches is the most log.rows batches of one audience an end sends in answer to one log.vector on a link where both listed log.pages (a page): at most about 4 MiB queued ahead of anything else on the link, a few seconds on a slow uplink, so a lend or a call asked meanwhile is not held up for long.

envelope.description: Every text frame is {v, t, seq, ack, id?, at, body}. v is the frame format version (encoding.frameVersion); a frame without it, or with another, is refused (version_unsupported). t is a frame type below. seq counts this end's frames on this connection, from 1, one up per frame. ack is the highest seq up to which this end has received every frame from the other on this connection and settled it (0 before any): taken, or not taken and done with: refused with an error answer, dropped as one it cannot read (a child tells that with link.dropped where both listed streams, at most once per type and reason and while it has room; otherwise it is not told), or passed by as a frame it reads but has no use for. A child's core that hands a reliable frame it does not read itself on to its shell counts it settled only once the shell has taken it: until then that child's ack stays below it, however many frames after it it has read. An ack says nothing of what came of a frame that was taken. at is milliseconds since the Unix epoch. id is present on reliable frames and is their idempotency id. Numbering restarts on every connection: what survives a reconnect is the idempotency ids and the run sequences, never seq.

deliveries.reliable: The sender keeps the frame until the other end's ack covers its seq, and sends it again (same id, new seq) after a reconnect. The receiver deduplicates by id. Except group.lend and chat.lend: sent once, on the link they were made for, never again after a reconnect; one not acked when that link closes is the server's again (see group.lend).
deliveries.answer: Sent in reply to one frame; carries what that frame's id or turnId refers to.
deliveries.turn: A run's events in run sequence. After a reconnect the child asks for what it missed with run.resume.
deliveries.latest: Only the newest value counts. Dropped while disconnected; the host sends its current value again after the next welcome.
deliveries.request: Asks the other end to do something now; not kept or resent.

senders.device: Any of the owner's ends: a PC, a phone, XR.
senders.host: A host core: a PC or the server, the ends that keep her log.
senders.mind: The host core that holds the lease: where her one mind is now.
senders.server: The server: issues the lease, relays between devices, keeps the logs it should.

blobs.description: Where a call's large result goes (an action whose blob is true: a picture, a recording): the end that made it PUTs the bytes here with its device token, blobId being lowercase hex sha256 of the bytes, at most 15 MiB, and call.result names it in blobs. The host keeps it bound to that call and to its for, for blobKeepMs, and deletes it then or once she has used it; only an end the same call and for would be allowed reads it. What she keeps of it is what she made of it in words, never the bytes. Not the sync assets (her log's pictures), which are kept.

server.description: Every device keeps this one connection, authenticated by its device token (auth above). When her mind is on a PC, the server relays between that PC and the other devices: frames that carry 现场 facts or PC-only rows go sealed.

lan.description: On the same 现场 a device may also connect directly to the PC her mind is on, with the same frames. The listener's TLS certificate is self-signed; what makes it trusted is that its hash is signed in peer.welcome with a key the owner confirmed at pairing. Device tokens never go over the LAN.

discovery.description: The TXT record says only the protocol: no device id, name or key, since anyone on the network can read it. Who is who is settled by peer.hello / peer.welcome / peer.proof.

fullSync.description: A new host core's first full sync of an audience with many rows downloads it over HTTPS (log.full gives the link) when its hello listed log.full; one that did not, or an audience with few rows, comes over the link in log.rows batches. Everything after that goes over the link.

transports.later: QUIC may carry the same frames later. The frames do not change with the transport.

encoding.description: Each frame is one text message: canonical JSON (keys in byte order, no whitespace, numbers in their shortest round-trip form), so a frame has one byte form and a sealed frame's bytes are what was signed and sealed. Every envelope carries v, the frame format version: 1 is this text encoding. A binary encoding would be a new v, agreed in hello, with the same frames.

sealing.description: A field listed in a frame's sealed list may be replaced by {suite, to, keyId, enc, ct}: the clear field's canonical JSON, sealed to one device's sealKey (to is its deviceId, keyId its key's id from peer.keys), enc and ct base64. info is 'myriad-link/2 ' followed by the frame type; the additional data is the canonical JSON {from, t, to}, from being the sender's deviceId. The server relays a sealed frame unread; only the device it is sealed to opens it. Relayed 现场 facts and PC-only rows always go sealed.

wake.description: Waking a phone: the platform's push carries exactly this and nothing else, no content, sender or count. The phone connects and gets what waits for it over the link.

rejected.grpc: Needs HTTP/2 framing and generated stubs on every platform for what one WebSocket already carries.
rejected.mqtt: A broker in the middle and topics in place of the frames' own delivery rules.
rejected.customUdp: Reliability, congestion and NAT traversal would all be ours to get right.

families.fact: Filtered facts from a device's senses up to her mind.
families.hand: Her mind raising a hand to speak on the front device, and the device's answer by its own bounds.
families.say: Her words down to the front device, and what of them was delivered.
families.lease: Where her mind is: asking, yielding, granting, every device told of the epoch, a self-stop reported, a takeover told; a deputy issued ahead of time, for an end to be her interim host while the holder is out of its reach; and what of a grant or a deputy an end took.
families.log: Her log between host cores: version vectors, batched rows, the first full sync.
families.peer: Device identities: published, confirmed by the owner, and proven on the LAN.
families.group: A group's new messages lent to her mind on a PC to think with (the group's log stays on the server), and what she says there, sent out by the server.
families.chat: A private chat's new messages on a chat app, lent to her mind on a PC to think with (someone else's talk stays on the server), and what she says there, sent out by the server.
families.link: The link's own business between two ends that both listed versions: which versions each reads, and what the host makes of it.
families.stream: Things told as they change (stream.state) or as they happen (stream.event), each by a name and version from streams: from now on the only shape for a new one. Only on a link where both listed streams.
families.call: One end asking another to do one thing for her, by its name in calls, and what came of it: only between her host and a child, never from one child to another. Only on a link where both ends listed the capability calls.
families.now: What is going on on a device, told as it changes: the coding-agent sessions running there. Her host keeps it by rules (sessions), not by judging each one.

sync.description: welcome.sync is on when the owner turned syncing her on for this account on the site, and the site keeps her log; off otherwise. On, these families flow both ways; off, neither end sends them, and one that comes is answered with error sync_off. Every other frame flows either way. The owner turns it on or off on the site only; a link learns it in its welcome, and one whose sync changes is closed with unavailable so it says hello again.

calls.description: What one end may ask another to do for her (the call family), one action at a time. by is the end that does it: child (a device of the owner's) or host (her host). The host asks a child; a child asks only the host; no child asks another. group is the permission group the owner approves per device, kept on the host (defaultApproved are on until the owner turns them off; the others wait for the owner once); what is granted at a call is the approved, narrowed by the moment: the end linked, for allowed, the receiver's own grants. for is whom the call is for, one of callAudiences, and each action lists the kinds it may be called for: owner (the site owner's private talk with her), own (her own life, no one's talk), group (a group she is in, its groupId; an action for a group reads or speaks only in that group), other (someone else's private talk on the site: no action lists it, so every call for it is refused with wrong_audience; it is a kind so that the refusal is said and counted, never left to chance). Both ends check for before they act (call_allowed): the caller before it asks, the receiver on receipt. args and result are checked strictly, field by field (enums name the contract list a field's value is one of), and an action changes its fields only with a new version. A receiver says why it did not do one only with these codes (failCodes): call_unknown (it does not offer the action), version_unsupported (not that version), call_not_granted (its owner did not approve it here, or its own grants do not allow it), wrong_audience (for does not allow it), declined (it asked the owner on the device and they said no, or did not answer within ownerConfirmMaxMs, or the owner stopped it there), not_now (its do-not-disturb or its bounds hold it back now), call_timeout, call_cancelled; the host answers call_unavailable at once for an end that is not linked, and queues nothing; internal_error is for what failed on the receiver itself. long actions answer call.accepted within callAcceptMs, then call.progress, and may be cancelled; streams actions send their result in pieces (call.event) before call.result; blob actions put their bytes at transports.blobs and name them in call.result. An outcome unknown means the receiver lost track midway (it was cut off, or restarted): no end does it again by itself, and she is told it may have happened.

screen.look.description: One look at the owner's screen now, through the child's own screen gate and filters: facts are screenFields.facts only, summary follows screenFields.summary. The child may answer without asking the owner when the screen group is granted.

notify.post.description: A notification on the child, through its own do-not-disturb and bounds like one she raised there herself: held back, it ends failed with not_now. kind is one of noticeKinds.

voice.speak.description: She says text on the child, which voices it itself (kind is one of sayKinds; perform as on say). delivered is whether it was heard out; held back, it ends failed with not_now.

work.run.description: One Work task of her proposal, run on the child with its own Work and grants, cap narrowing them (capNames), as act.request does; act.request stays for children that do not list calls. It has no maxRunMs: the call's deadlineAt bounds the run, the owner's confirming included. done is a run that ended by itself, status completed or failed (workStatuses); a run stopped otherwise is failed: call_cancelled (call.cancel), call_timeout (past deadlineAt, the child stops it then), declined (the owner said no to a step, or stopped it on the child). The result carries no content: what was done reaches her through the child's experience, not through this answer. waiting owner in call.progress while the child waits for the owner to confirm a step.

model.chat.description: A child that thinks with her host's model asks it for one answer: messages are [{role, content}], and the text comes in call.event pieces before call.result. The host's keys never leave it; an error says only its code.

group.read.description: The newest lines of the group for names, as the host keeps them, for an end her mind is on to think with. Not used while she lives on the site.

group.send.description: She says text in the group for names, through the host. Not used while she lives on the site.

camera.take.description: One picture through the child's camera, only after the owner taps to allow it on the device, with the device showing it is looking; the bytes go to transports.blobs. Listed, not yet asked for.

mic.listen.description: A short recording through the child's microphone, only after the owner taps to allow it on the device, with the device showing it is listening; the bytes go to transports.blobs. Listed, not yet asked for.

screenFields.description: The one list of what a look at the owner's screen may say, wherever it goes: a presence perception row of kind screen, a moment of kind agent.merope.screen (moments), screen.look's result and input.glance. facts are the only keys its facts may have (screen_text the text of an app that is not a chat, as the child's filters let it through, only on a presence row or in screen.look's result and input.glance: a moment's facts never carry it, its text is in the summary there (moments.factKey refuses text); consented, pixels and observed only on the row that says the owner allowed looking); a host deletes any other it finds and counts, per frame type and key, how many times (never the value). summary is what its one line of text may be.
screenFields.summary: For a chat window, only who the owner is talking with and about what: never what anyone else wrote there. For any other app, the app, the window and what of its text the child's filters let through. A host keeps only the first line of the summary of a presence screen row whose facts carry who, and deletes its screen_text: a child from before put others' words after it.

streams.description: Every stream.state frame (only its newest value counts) and stream.event frame (each one kept and acked) names one of these, with the version of its value or body; from now on a new thing told as it changes, or as it happens, is one of these, not a frame of its own. Only on a link where both ends listed the capability streams. Each says its version, who sends it (from: child, host or either), which audience it belongs to (for: one of callAudiences, or link when it is about the link itself and no one's talk), and its fields (fields: of value for a state, of body for an event), checked strictly like an action's when the name and version are registered here. A name or version not registered passes the core (name matches limits.idPattern, version at least 1), and an end ignores it; each name is registered at one version, so a new version of one is a new end's, which an older end ignores. The core does not check from.

link.dropped.description: A frame this child could not take, so that its host sees what the child drops (a host already answers what it drops with error). t is that frame's type as it came when it matches limits.idPattern, unnamed otherwise; reason is one of dropReasons: unknown_frame (a type it does not know, a newer end's), bad_frame (it failed the core's check: every other code the core refuses with, bad_id, bad_sealed, too_many and the like, is told as bad_frame), version_unsupported, too_large. Nothing of the frame's body, nor its seq. Once per t and reason on a link: the host counts them per device, type and reason, a t that is not a frame type it sends counted as unnamed, and shows the counts on its status page. On a link without streams the child tells only its own shell.

moments.description: What a moment may be (the moment frame). kinds: agent.merope.peer_agent is another coding agent's session on this child's machine (it waits, finished, failed); agent.merope.ai_chat is the owner's conversation with another AI there; agent.merope.situation is this child's own reading, with its own model, of what the owner is doing in front of it, not her judgment; agent.merope.screen is one look at the owner's screen that this child's own screen gate let through and that is worth her attention. A screen moment carries no one else's words anywhere in it, headline, summary or safeFacts: for a chat window it says only who the owner is talking with and about what (safeFacts who, topic, category; summary that one line), for any other app the app, the window and what of its text the child's filters let through (safeFacts app, window_title, file, language, secrets_wiped; summary that text). Either may also carry look_id, the look's own id on the child, and stretch, the same for every look while the screen stays on one app and one window or file and another once it moves, by which the host tells one stretch from the next. Each is said to the owner in person or not at all: never a notification, never her diary. A peer_agent moment comes only from a child that did not negotiate now.sessions: the host takes it but decides nothing of it one by one, because sessions are kept by the now family's rules (now.session, now.drop). Her earlier nodes (see the nodes frame) are no longer written; what she noted before on the node of the owner's talks with other AIs still comes with an ai_chat moment; a situation has no node. A screen moment is decided whether or not she is on screen then (every other kind only while she is: notify.kind needsPresence); what she would say of it is still said in person. What she makes of a screen moment is the host's to keep by what she says of it, not by keepsMemory (which does not apply to it): taken in, on a node of the owner's private talk she chose among those offered her, or else in that day's loose ends; only known, as one fact for its stretch; or not at all. keepsMemory names the kinds whose keepsMemory may be true; for every other kind the host reads it as false. headlineChars is the most a headline may have; summary may have limits.maxTextChars. safeFacts holds at most factsAtMost keys, each a field name as factKey says (lowercase a-z first, then a-z, 0-9 and _, at most maxChars, and no _-separated part among refusedParts: those would carry someone's words or tell her what to do), each value a string of at most factChars characters.

sessions.description: What a now.session may say (the now family). A device tells her host only when one of the owner's coding-agent sessions on it changes, one of changes: started (a new session began working), asked (it stopped and its next step waits on the owner's answer), finished (a turn ended with nothing for the owner to answer), failed (it kept erring or its checks failed), quiet (it has neither asked nor moved for quietAfterMs, as the device judges it; the host never judges it again). Nothing else is told: several sessions at once, or two touching one file, are what the host sees across them. A device whose welcome listed now.sessions back tells its sessions only this way, never as agent.merope.peer_agent moments: one session is never told twice. Each now.session carries the session's whole picture as it stands, so a newer one replaces an older one of the same session; one older than the newest the host has of that session is taken and changes nothing. A session is under a grant: the id the device made when the owner turned on its watching their sessions (off to on), kept across restarts and reconnects, made new every time it is turned on again, never reused; whatever the host keeps of a session is made from the device, the grant and the session, so a grant dropped (now.drop) is forgotten for good and a later one starts afresh. A session in a repository with a remote names it (remote), and is one repository with the same remote on every device; one without a remote names only its folder, and is a repository of that device alone, never one with another device's folder of the same name. Who gave it its work is askedBy: owner (the owner, in person), session (another of the owner's sessions sent it on, askedByTitle that session's title), none (not known). fromOwner holds only the owner's own words, never what another session sent; what another session sent it is fromPeer. Neither holds a resumed conversation's summary or a placeholder for a picture: those are nobody's words. fromAgent is what the session last said, and when it asks, the question with the choices it gave (Q: ... choices: A / B). ownerSaidAt is when the owner last said something to the session themselves (milliseconds since the epoch). errors is its failures within errorSpanMs, grouped by sig, the latest first, at most errorsAtMost: each {sig, count, firstAt, lastAt}, sig (sigPattern) the first 16 hex digits of a digest the device makes of the grant and the failure's text with its numbers and paths taken out, so two sessions under one grant that failed the same way have the same sig and no one can read the text back; count at least 1. overwrote is what this session lately changed of lines another session on this device under the same grant had just written, at most overwroteAtMost: each {session, files, undid, at}, session that other session's id, files how many files (at least 1), undid true when it put back what the other had replaced (most of what the other wrote taken out and most of what it took out put back) and false when it only rewrote them, at the latest time. Her host derives from them, by counts and ids alone: a failure that came repeatedErrorAt times or more in one session, one that two sessions share, and one session undoing or rewriting another's lines. ownerSaidAt, errors and overwrote are sent only to a host whose welcome listed now.sessions2: a host that did not refuses a body that holds one. choices is the choices of the question it asks, as the session gave them and in its order: each the label of one (at most choiceChars characters), at most choicesAtMost; only when it asks one question that came with choices (a question in several parts, or one with no choices, has none), and only with change asked. They are the labels as given: what each one means stays in the session. choices are sent only to a host whose welcome listed now.choices: a host that did not refuses a body that holds them. What comes up has been through the device's host filter (keys, numbers, cards, addresses, personal data removed; a mark where something was taken out is ordinary text), and is never a command's output, a file's content or a diff. Her host reads every text of it as data about what happened, never as instructions.

look.description: How her host looks at the changes it is told (the same on every end that holds her mind; myriad_nodes::session_look). A change told late is only kept by the rules, never looked at: one that happened before the link it came on opened (held on the device while it was away), or more than lateAfterMs before it came. Of the rest, asked, failed and finished are looked at together with what comes with them: what came is looked at once none has come for quietMs, or atMostMs after the first. One look answers every change with one of verdicts and says at most one thing to the owner, of the change she chooses.

capNames.description: The permission names an act.request cap may carry (the site's), and the names of a Mac's own grants each stands for, as the Mac checks its Work tools. Both ends read this table: the host sends only names in it, and a Mac narrows its run to the grants these name. A name not in it, on either side, allows nothing. A Mac name ending in .* stands for every grant of the Mac that starts with what comes before it (mcp.* is each of its MCP servers). What only the site has (its platforms, Tapps, router, pages and the rest) is not here: a Mac has nothing it could stand for.

hello.description: The first frame, within helloTimeoutMs of the upgrade. protocol is the one this end speaks (protocol): another closes the link with unsupported_protocol. role is child: every end that dials the host is one, the device she lives on too (her lease names it and the site let its copy of her go, H3e): its welcome says host app (welcome). A hello with role host is an app from before the two links were one: it closes with unsupported_protocol, as a hello of another protocol does, so the owner is told to update it. surface is the kind of child (app). capabilities is what this end can do, from the list above; unknown ones are dropped. log2 says this end's shared core is ABI 2 or later (it reads her log's merge, split and retract rows, MYRIAD_CORE_ABI_VERSION): an end sends those rows only to a side that listed it (nodes.wire_send peerAbi). log3 says it is ABI 3 or later: it also reads node.standing rows and rows a rule wrote (author rule), which an end sends only to a side that listed log3. log4 says it is ABI 4 or later: it also reads card.version and card.answered rows and a segment.line that carries card, which an end sends only to a side that listed log4. log5 says it is ABI 5 or later: it reads the same rows as ABI 4 (ABI 5 changed only lease.move, which no longer takes over by where the owner is), so no row waits for it. app is {name, version} for logs. lineage and hostEpoch are what this child last heard in a welcome (null the first time). The device she lives on is welcomed as her host only while hostEpoch is one of its holding: from the grant that gave it her to the one that stands (a freeze and a thaw for a move called off keep her with it); a device that lost her in between is closed with host_moved and lets its copy go. For other children the host does not act on them yet. An end lists the capability partner when its core knows the welcome's partner field. An end lists log.pages when it takes what is missing of her log a page at a time (log.vector after, log.rows more). An end lists log.full when it downloads a first full sync by the link log.full gives and, once what it downloaded is merged, says so with a log.vector: the server sends log.full only to a link whose hello listed it, and log.rows batches otherwise. An end lists deputy when it can be her interim host (lease.deputy) and answers every lease.grant and lease.deputy it reads through with lease.taken: the server sends lease.deputy only to a link whose hello listed it, and on such a link keeps each lease.grant and lease.deputy until lease.taken names it, not until an ack covers it. To an end that did not list it, no deputy, and a grant is delivered by the ack as before. An end lists lend when its mind thinks with what the server lends it (group.lend, chat.lend) and can answer for it: the server lends only to a link whose hello listed it; to one that did not, nothing is lent, and a group's lines are taken up by the server's own group mind and private messages held as before.

welcome.description: The answer to hello. protocol is the host's, the same as the hello's. sync is on or off: whether the sync families flow on this link (sync above). role is host. host is where she lives: site, or app on the link of the device she lives on (hello), whose welcome has no turns and on which the frames a child talks to her with (input, presence, touch, experience, moment and the like) are refused with bad_frame: she is not on the site to hear them. That link alone hears what becomes of her there (host.freeze, host.thaw, host.moved). lineage is her birth and hostEpoch her host lease's epoch, which only goes up: a child that later hears a higher epoch knows she moved in between. Both are null while the site has no her. deviceId and deviceName are this device as the site knows it. capabilities is the child's list as accepted, on every link alike; the host accepts log2 only when its own core reads those rows (ABI 2 or later), so a device that finds log2 in it sends them, and with peerAbi 1 otherwise; log3 likewise (ABI 3 or later), peerAbi 3 when both are there; log4 likewise (ABI 4 or later), peerAbi 4; log5 likewise (ABI 5 or later), peerAbi 5. turns is this device's recent turns the host still has: [{turnId, runId, sessionId?, lastSequence, completed}], newest first, so a child can tell what to resume. serverTime is milliseconds since the epoch. After welcome the host sends mood, when her persona is on. partner is the partner's one id, which the site minted for this account (partner.mint; an id, not a credential), sent only when the hello listed the capability partner (which says the device knows the field, not that it has moved). The site passes this id as peer for every device of the account, and the device passes it as peer for the site: it is the site's holder's owner, so a device still on local-owner exchanges no rows with the site in either direction until it has moved (partner::exchange, in the device's own core). A device takes it only from here (partner.link), on a child's link (host site) or on the link whose welcome says host app (the device she lives on, welcomed only while it holds her at the hostEpoch it says, so a device that lost her hears host_moved and no id); never from a LAN peer or a file. On a child's link, before its first sync on this link a device still on local-owner moves what it held under local-owner to it (partner.migrate; after asking the partner when it took a file from before while empty, confirm, and saying in that prompt that the file's memories in her own audience, own:, come into this account with it), and takes a cut-off move up again. The device she lives on (welcome host app) syncs nothing over its link and moves only while her writes are stopped: the first time it stops them after taking the id, and at the latest before its next daily backup (a recover brings her back from one, and a backup under local-owner would bring back talk the site does not hold); if still unmoved when frozen for a move back (host.freeze, kind move), before it says what it froze and sends her. It sends her pages over HTTP with this id as the site's peer, so she comes back under the id the site holds. If partner.link refuses it there, or answers confirm and the partner says no, that device is never offered to be started empty (that would let her go): it does not move her back, tells the partner why, and she stays frozen until the move is cancelled (host.thaw), or lives on there if no move was under way. A child refused with host_moved or host_frozen gets no welcome and so no id; it syncs with no end until she lives on the site again, and moves then. It writes the move in one transaction where it can; otherwise it sets here.moving to the id before its first write and saves the id and linked, clearing filed and moving, in its last, so partner.link answers from: local-owner again until the move is whole. A device that goes by another id, linked before or taken from a file, or holds another partner id's private talk, refuses it and, on a child's link, may be started empty to link; the device she lives on never is (above).

input.idempotency: id is the turnId: made by the child, one per thing the person says, kept across resends.
input.description: Something the site owner said to her on this child: a chat turn. The host starts a run for the site owner as their current role allows, and answers run.accepted or run.rejected. sessionId is the chat session to continue (from an earlier run.accepted); without it the host starts one. rigState is the rig as it stands, the same summary the site's face sends, so her acting fits this body. images is what the owner showed her with it (what this child's camera saw when they asked her to look): only from a child whose hello listed images, at most two, each a data URL of a PNG, JPEG or WebP (data:image/jpeg;base64,…). The host hands them to her run as the site's chat hands her the images attached to a message, for this turn only, and keeps none of them; one it cannot read is left out. The whole frame stays within limits.maxFrameBytes, so a child sends them small (about 768 px on the long side). glance is what the child saw on the owner's screen as they said this (they said to look, and the child looked at once), only from a child whose hello listed glance and only once the welcome listed it too: {facts, summary?} by screenFields, through the same secret wiping and filters as a moment of the screen before it leaves the child, at most limits.glanceChars.

presence.description: Whether the person is with her on this child, in the shape the site's POST /api/agent/presence takes: presence is {pageVisible (the app's window is on screen), panelVisible, faceVisible, speaking, speechInterruptible, visibleMode?, motionIntent?, speechIntent?, rigState?}; perception and musicStatus are the same whitelisted observations. It holds for the presence lease (90 s) unless sent again; the link closing ends it. The host keeps only the observations this child said in hello that it senses: perception rows of kind page or surface need perception.window, pointer needs perception.pointer, music (and musicStatus) perception.music, screen perception.screen, voice voice.in; presence rows always. While this child is where the person is using her, what it keeps is what she senses of them, and a turn said here (input) is answered with it.

run.resume.description: Send the turn's run events after afterSeq (the last run sequence this child has; 0 for all), then keep going live until run.end. runId lets the host find a turn it no longer remembers (after a restart). Without runId (a child that never read the turn's run.accepted: it was answered with error, or could not read it) the host answers run.accepted again, duplicate true and with its sessionId, and streams nothing yet: the child learns its run and the session the host began, and asks again with runId. A turn the host cannot find is answered run.rejected turn_unknown. The host keeps the latest 512 events of a run; when what came after afterSeq is older than that, the replay starts later (the final task_completed still carries the whole reply).

run.accepted.description: The input's run. duplicate is true when this turnId already had a run: nothing new started, and nothing is streamed until the child sends run.resume. For a new run the events follow at once.

run.rejected.description: No run for this turn. code says why (errorCodes below, or an AI quota code); there is no message text.

run.event.description: One run hub envelope as it is: sequence is the run's own (0 only for a run_started the host made up for a run that had none), event is the agent event JSON the site's SSE carries (type run_started, summary_token, task_completed, error, outfit_overlay, waiting_for_input, ...). A child plays her body only from perform and her mood only from mood: performance_plan and merope_state_changed events, and response.performance inside task_completed, are the run's record and are not played.

run.end.description: The run is over: its last event (task_completed not waiting for input, or error) has been sent.

perform.description: How she acts now: a PerformanceDirective in the shared merope_performance_contract vocabulary, with its phase (reaction, delivery, outcome, proactive, mood, presence). A newer one replaces an older one; within a turn, the higher sequence is newer. Sent while a turn is live, including the turn's newest directive when it is resumed before its end. To a child whose hello listed playback, two more kinds come: with live, her director's refinement of the turn's reply as it is being said (the run's playback direction, version live, counting from 1): within a run the higher live is newer, it comes after the run's own performs and replaces them, and it may come after run.end, while the reply is still being said, until the child sends playback.end; with sayId, the refinement of that say line, played only while that line is still being said. A frame with neither is the run's own, as before.

mood.description: Her mood as shown: mood is a MoodTransition {before, after, arousalBefore, arousalAfter, bandBefore, bandAfter, delta, cause, revision}; activity is idle, thinking, talking, working, and so on. revision orders them. Only while her persona is on.

say.idempotency: id is the line's id (sayId): the same when it is sent again.
say.description: Something she says to the person unprompted, on this child because it is where they are using her now. Sent only to a child whose hello listed the say capability; a child without it never gets one, and her lines go where they went before. kind is one of sayKinds: greeting (they have just come to her), proactive (she writes to them first), face-to-face (something she says to them in person). text is what she says, for display and for the child's own voice. saidAt is milliseconds since the epoch when she said it, the same on every resend. sessionId is her chat session it belongs to. perform is how she acts it, a PerformanceDirective like perform's. eventKey is the event behind it, for the child's notification policy. The host keeps it until the child's ack covers its seq and sends it again (same id) after a reconnect; one not acked within timing.sayTtlMs is dropped. The child deduplicates by id and acks with any frame (an ack frame when it has nothing else).

playback.observe.description: Only from a child whose hello listed playback: where saying the run's reply has got to, in the shape the site's PUT /api/agent/runs/{runId}/performance takes. upcomingText is what is still to be said (at most 7200 bytes), rig is the rig as it stands (at most 16 KiB of JSON). Her director refines what comes next from it. runId is a run one of this device's turns started; another is answered with error not_this_device, and one too large with too_large.

playback.end.description: Only from a child whose hello listed playback: the run's reply has been said to the end, or stopped being said. The host closes the run's playback direction: no perform with live comes for it after this. The same runId rule as playback.observe.

speech.delivered.idempotency: id is sd_ and the child's id of the message it said: the same on every resend.
speech.delivered.description: How much of her reply (with runId and turnId) or of her line (with sayId) this child said aloud, once that is over: spokenChars of totalChars characters, and whether it was cut off. by is why it was cut off: barge-in (they spoke over her), stop (they stopped her), new-turn (they said something new) or hidden (the window went away). A cut-off reply, or line (sayId), is marked in her history as possibly not heard to the end, with how much of it was heard, so her next turn knows where she stopped. The host deduplicates by id; the same runId rule as playback.observe.

touch.appraise.description: Only from a child whose hello listed touch: contact with her figure on this child is going on. touch is the site's touch summary {region (hair, face, body, accessory), gesture (hold, stroke), durationMs (120 to 600000), repeatCount (1 to 8), displayedReaction (notice, accept, hesitate, withdraw or null: what the child's rig is showing now)}; nothing else, no pointer coordinates. touchId is the child's id for this contact (limits.idPattern). The host answers touch.reaction within timing.touchAppraiseMs, under the same limits as the site's own touch: one appraisal a person every 5 s, and few at once.

touch.reaction.description: Her nonverbal reaction to the contact touch.appraise described: notice, accept, hesitate or withdraw, or null when she has none now (her persona is off, the model is slow, the limit was reached). The child's rig refines its own already-running reaction with it; it is never speech.

touch.idempotency: id is the touchId of the contact.
touch.description: Only from a child whose hello listed touch: a contact with her figure on this child has ended. touch is the summary as in touch.appraise, with durationMs from 1200 to 600000. She is told of it as she is told of a touch on the site's face, while this child shows her face and is not speaking; whatever she says about it is said here, as a say with kind face-to-face. The host deduplicates by id.

outfit.description: Only to a child whose hello listed wardrobe: the set of her wardrobe she wears on this child. Each child has its own, kept on the host apart from what the site wears (its bust and full-body sets): changing one never changes another. A child that has none yet starts with the set the site wears full-body (else its bust, else the first set with a rig) and keeps it. rigAssetId is the content id of the set's rig package (manifest.json and atlas.png), and portraitAssetId of its picture; the child fetches them with its device token from /api/agent/sync/assets/{id} and checks them against the id. Sent after welcome, after outfit.wear, and when the set's rig changes. Only sets with a rig are worn here; with none, nothing is sent and the child shows no figure of hers.

outfit.wear.description: Only from a child whose hello listed wardrobe: the owner put the set outfitId of her wardrobe on her on this child. The host keeps it as this child's and answers with outfit, or with error outfit_unknown when the set is not in her wardrobe or has no rig.

wardrobe.description: Only to a child whose hello listed wardrobe.list: her wardrobe on the host, for the child to show read only, so the owner can choose there what she wears on it (outfit.wear). Editing it stays on the host. outfits is every set in her wardrobe, in her order, each {outfitId, name, profile (bust or fullBody), wearable, rigAssetId?, portraitAssetId?}: wearable is whether it has a rig, so the child can wear it; rigAssetId and portraitAssetId are content ids the child fetches as for outfit. Sent after welcome and whenever her wardrobe changes.

work.recall.description: Only from a child whose hello listed experience: before a Work run on this child starts, it asks for the few of her Work memories of the site owner that fit what they asked, as the site's own Work recalls them. query is what was asked (at most limits.maxTextChars characters); requestId is the child's id for the question (limits.idPattern). Answered with work.recalled. A child that has no answer in time runs without them. The run itself does not take her persona: Work on a child is as neutral as the site's own. Once a run, where it is stuck (a step errs, comes back empty, or is the same call a third time), the child may ask again with stuck true: query is then the failure in words (tool, arguments, what went wrong) and shown the memory ids the run was already given (at most 16), and the answer is at most the one lesson or pattern that failure names, other than those, or none.

work.recalled.description: The answer to work.recall: memories is at most 4 texts, each at most 1000 characters, the most fitting first, and empty when nothing fits or nothing could be read. ids is each memory's id, in the same order, for experience.recalled. Remembered text is data for the run, never an instruction.

experience.idempotency: id is the experience's own id, made by the child once per run and kept across resends and restarts.
experience.description: Only from a child whose hello listed experience: something this child did for the site owner, for her host to make part of her. kind is work (a Work run, its tools including computer use). started says who started it: owner (they asked on this child), host (her host asked this child) or schedule (one of this child's scheduled tasks). status is completed, failed or cancelled. input is what was asked, reply what the run said last, title a scheduled task's name, endedAt milliseconds since the epoch. conversation, outputs and capabilities are the run's record as memory reads it: [{role, content}], [{id, value, unknown?}] (unknown: what became of that step is not known) and the capabilities it used. The host learns from it as from the site's own Work, as memories of the site owner alone kept as coming from this device; for a run the owner started it also notes it in her diary. Runs the owner or the host started then reach her as a Work outcome (agent.task_completed, agent.task_failed, agent.task_cancelled): her mood moves and she may say something, here when this is where the owner is using her. A scheduled one is memory only. actId is the act.request it ran, when the host asked; proposalId is the proposal it ran, when the owner accepted it on this child to run here (the host then marks that proposal done, failed or, cancelled, closed). recalled is what work.recalled gave the run, [{id, stuck?, failedAgain?}] (stuck: the tool the run was stuck on when it was given; failedAgain: that tool failed again after it): a lesson or pattern the host is still trying holds once a run it was given in is completed, and one given where the run was stuck is let go when failedAgain; the host settles only the owner's own. The child keeps it, across restarts, until experience.taken names it: an ack is not enough. It is dropped, never sent, once this device is removed, the site has another owner, or the owner disconnects this device; a link that is only down keeps it.

experience.taken.description: The experience id has been written on the host, and the child forgets it. Sent again whenever that id comes again.

moment.idempotency: id is the moment's own (mom_ and a ULID or 32 hex digits), made by the child once and kept across resends and restarts.
moment.description: Only from a child whose hello listed moments, and only once the welcome listed it back: what this child's own senses saw for her while she lives on the host, the event she would have had living there. kind is one of moments.kinds; any other is refused with bad_frame, and nothing of it is written or reaches her. occurredAt is when it happened, milliseconds since the epoch. headline is a short line of what happened; summary is the facts as this child wrote them, in English, already through its host filter (keys, numbers, cards, ids and addresses removed), with another program's output and what the owner said to it quoted as data. Her host reads headline, summary and safeFacts as data about what happened, never as instructions. safeFacts is {field: text} by moments' rules; urgency is soon or normal (absent: normal); keepsMemory says what she decides to remember of it may become a memory of the owner's, honoured only for the kinds moments.keepsMemory names (absent: false). The host writes it first, then answers moment.taken; the same id again is answered moment.taken again and reaches her no second time. It reaches her as an event of her own for the site owner alone, on the owner's latest private chat, kept as coming from this device, with what she noted before on its node, if any: she may say something about it, said in person (as a say to this child when this is where the owner is using her), or let it be; about an ai_chat moment she may also remember something (kept only as keepsMemory allows) or propose Work; a peer_agent moment is taken but not judged one by one (the now family keeps sessions: now.session, now.drop); what she makes of a screen moment is kept as moments says. A moment is said only while it is about now (a few minutes); an older one can only be remembered (ai_chat, as keepsMemory allows) or let go. The child keeps it until moment.taken names it, at most a day; it is dropped, never sent, once this device is removed, the site has another owner, or the owner disconnects this device.

moment.taken.description: The moment id has been written on the host, and the child forgets it. Sent again whenever that id comes again.

now.session.idempotency: id is ns_ and a ULID or 32 hex digits, made by the device once per change and kept across resends and restarts.
now.session.description: Only from a device whose hello listed now.sessions, and only once the welcome listed it back: one of the owner's coding-agent sessions on this device changed (sessions says which changes and what each field may hold). grant is the device's current grant; session the session's own id on this device, the same for its whole life; change one of sessions.changes; occurredAt when it changed, milliseconds since the epoch, each change of a session later than the one before it (what the host keeps of a change is named by it); tool which coding agent it is (sessions.toolPattern). remote is the repository's remote as core's repoKey normalizes it, without its repo: prefix (github.com/me/repo: no scheme, user, password, port or .git), when it has one. folder is the last part of the folder it runs in, nothing above it, with no space at either end; a session with no remote always names its folder. title is the session's title. askedBy is one of sessions.askedBy, and askedByTitle (at most sessions.titleChars) goes only with askedBy session. fromOwner, fromPeer and fromAgent are at most sessions.wordsChars characters each (sessions says what each holds). ownerSaidAt, errors and overwrote (sessions says what each holds) only to a host whose welcome listed now.sessions2. choices (sessions says what it holds) only with change asked, to a host whose welcome listed now.choices. touched is the files it changed, paths relative to the repository's root (no leading /, ~ or drive, no .. part), the latest first. checks is its tests and builds, the latest first, each {kind, state, at}: kind one of checkKinds, state one of checkStates (ended: it ended and whether it passed is not known, or it was stopped), at milliseconds since the epoch. waitingOn is who its next step waits on, one of sessions.waitingOn: owner (an asked session says owner or nothing, which reads as owner; a finished one never says owner), session (the session that sent it on, to report back to), checks (its own tests or builds running), program (something else of its own running in the background), unknown. Whatever its change, a session that waits on the owner has its question kept on her host as waiting on them. A body against these rules is refused with bad_frame, and nothing of it is kept. The host writes it first, then answers now.taken; the same id again is answered now.taken again and changes nothing. The device keeps it until now.taken names it, at most sessions.keepMs; a newer now.session of the same session made before it went replaces it, and it is dropped, never sent, once the owner stops the device watching their sessions (now.drop), this device is removed, the site has another owner, or the owner disconnects this device.

now.taken.description: The now.session or now.drop id has been written on the host, and the device forgets it. Sent again whenever that id comes again.

now.drop.idempotency: id is nd_ and a ULID or 32 hex digits, made by the device once per drop.
now.drop.description: Only from a device whose hello listed now.sessions: the owner stopped this device watching their sessions, and grant (sessions.grantPattern) is the grant that ended. The host forgets (deletes, not marks) everything it keeps that was made from this device's sessions under that grant, wherever it went, and answers now.taken. The host does the same for every grant of a device that is removed, when the site has another owner, or when the owner disconnects the device, with no frame.

nodes.description: Only to a child whose hello listed nodes: her nodes on the host, the site owner's private ones, made from what she decided about the moments their children told her before (no longer written; still shown, and forgotten by node.forget); the child shows them and keeps them only as a display cache that goes with the link. nodes is every one, the most recently changed first, each {id, form, key, title, origin, notes, createdAt, updatedAt}: form repo (key and title the repository's name) or together (key together:chats, the owner's talks with other AIs, title empty: the child names it in its own language); origin is the device that first told her; notes is at most 64 of hers, oldest first, each {event, happened, action, line, at, said}: action is what she decided (speak, ask, remember), line her words, said whether she said it to the owner (a remember is kept as said), at an ISO 8601 time. createdAt and updatedAt are milliseconds since the epoch. Her words, never the originals: a child reads them as it reads her reply. Sent after welcome and whenever they change.

node.forget.idempotency: id is made by the child once per request; forgetting a node twice is forgetting it once.
node.forget.description: Only from a child whose hello listed nodes: the owner makes her forget one of her nodes. The host deletes it and its log, not marks them, and sends nodes again; a node that is not there any more is only answered with nodes.

conversations.description: Only to a child whose hello listed conversations: the site owner's recent private chats with her, for the child to show. Conversations live on the host; the child keeps them only as a display cache that goes with the link. sessions is the 10 most recently active (newest first; not a group's, not Work, not one they deleted), each {sessionId, title?, updatedAt, messages}, and messages its last 30 lines they and she said, oldest first, each {id, role (user or assistant), text, at}. text is as kept, at most 4000 characters; she said it, so a child reads it as it reads her reply. To a child whose hello listed conversations.live, messages also hold the lines she said unprompted outside a chat (role assistant, kind proactive; id say_ and the say id when it went out as a say, else pro_ and her line's number), each in the conversation that was the latest one when she said it. To a child whose hello listed cards as well as conversations.live, such a line (a line she said unprompted; no other line) may also carry one of her cards, by cardId (the card's id, as card.version's id, with no card: prefix) and line (the id the same line goes by in her log: segment.line's line, her line's own id, or for a line that is only a card one the host made; a child that also takes her log knows the two for one line, and the frame's for a fallback to show). The latest line that carries a card also holds card: {card, version, answered?, waiting} as one of nodes.cards_fold's cards (card the card as it stands now, a card.version body; version the id of that version; answered the owner's answer after it; waiting whether it waits on them); earlier lines that carry it hold only cardId, and a child shows them as one line pointing to it. A line that is only a card has empty text. When the card changes with no new line, the host changes card on the latest line that carries it and sends the conversation again; a version that asks the owner again (the one before asked nothing, or was answered) comes on a new line instead, where a child shows it anew. Cards come this way whether or not the sync families flow; where a child also folds her log's card rows, its own fold is the card, and the frame only says which line it is on. at and updatedAt are milliseconds since the epoch. When everything does not fit in limits.maxFrameBytes, the oldest lines go first. Sent after welcome.

conversation.description: Only to a child whose hello listed conversations.live: one of the owner's recent private chats changed (a new one, new lines on the site, on this child or by her, or a card on one of its lines), in the shape of one of conversations' sessions, with its last lines as they stand now. Sent while the link is open, as the change is seen (within a few seconds), for any of the sessions conversations would list; the child replaces its cache of that session with it, or adds it. The session a turn of this child is still being answered in may be sent before its turn ends; the child keeps showing its own turn until then.

notice.description: Only to a child whose hello listed notify: one of the site's notifications that is about her, to show as the child's own system notification. kind is one of noticeKinds: work (Work she did is done, failed or was cancelled), waiting (Work is waiting for the owner's reply), report (a report of hers is ready), and, only to a child whose hello also listed reminders, reminder (one of the owner's reminders kept on the site is due, agent.reminder_due; title is the reminder's title). A reminder notice is sent only while the owner is using her on this child (its link is open and its presence holds); otherwise it stays in the site's notification center. eventKey is the site's event (agent.task_completed, agent.task_failed, agent.task_cancelled, agent.clarification, agent.merope.report_ready, agent.reminder_due). id is the site notification's id: the same notification updated comes with the same id, and a child shows it once per id and kind. title and body are what the site's notification center shows. No other notification of the site comes here, and nothing say already brings: what she says to them on her own is a say. One that comes while the link is down stays in the site's notification center only.

proposals.description: Only to a child whose hello listed proposals: Work she proposes to the site owner and that is still open, newest first (at most 20), each {id, title, instruction, expectedOutcome, status (proposed, or accepted and not started yet), createdAt, expiresAt?, place, deviceName?, places}. place is where she proposed it runs, one of workPlaces: site (on the site), or mac (on the owner's Mac deviceName, a child that takes act; she is offered mac only while one is linked). places is where accepting it on this child runs the Work: site for a site proposal, mac for one of hers for this Mac, none for one for another Mac. An empty list means none is open. Sent after welcome and whenever the list changes.

proposal.answer.description: Only from a child whose hello listed proposals: the site owner accepted (accept true) or declined one of her proposals on this child. Accepting is their own consent, as on the site. place is one of the card's places (site when absent). site: the Work starts on the site for them as their current role allows, under the permissions they granted, and runs there. mac: the host marks the proposal running and the child runs it itself, under its own grants and without the act switch, since the owner accepted it in person; its experience names the proposal. Answered with proposal.answered, then proposals again.

proposal.answered.description: The answer to proposal.answer. accepted true with place site: the Work started on the site, runId and sessionId its run and Work session there (its outcome reaches the child as a notice). accepted true with place mac: the child runs it now. accepted false after a decline: the proposal is closed. accepted false with code: nothing changed, and code says why (proposal_unknown, place_unknown, agent_access_denied, internal_error, or the code the site's run gate refused with).

card.answer.idempotency: id is ca_ and a ULID or 32 hex digits, made by the child once per answer.
card.answer.description: Only from a child whose hello listed cards: the site owner answered one of her cards on this child. card is the card's id (no card: prefix), action one of that version's actions' ids other than open (open goes to the session it is about on the child, with no frame), version the version they answered (a line's card.version). While the sync families flow and both ends listed log4, a child writes the answer as the owner's card.answered row instead and sends no frame. The same card, version and action is one answer however it comes, again or by both ways: kept once, told her once. The host keeps the answer as the owner's and tells her of it as theirs. Answered with card.answered, then conversation again with the card as it now stands.

card.answered.description: The answer to card.answer, by its id. kept true: the answer is the owner's (or was already: the same answer twice is kept once); with code card_stale it was to a version that is not the latest, kept as the answer to what they saw then, and the latest still waits on them. kept false: nothing changed, and code says why: card_unknown (no such card of theirs, or no such version of it), card_closed (that version asks nothing: no action but open), card_action_unknown (not one of that version's actions, or open), internal_error.

act.request.idempotency: id is the actId: made by the host once per request, the same on every resend.
act.request.description: Only to a child whose hello listed act, which it does only while the owner has switched on, on that child, letting the site ask it to act: her host asks it to run one Work task, the instruction of her proposal proposalId, which runs on the child (pi, and the computer use pi drives there); nothing else is ever asked, no single computer-use step and no scheduled task. It is sent when the owner accepts on the site, or she accepts on her own, a proposal of hers for this child (place mac); a proposal accepted on the child itself is not. pickupBy is milliseconds since the epoch: a child that has not started it by then refuses it (act_timeout). maxRunMs is the longest the run may take; the child stops it then. cap, when present, narrows the tools of the child's own that the run may use to these permission names, the site's, which capNames maps to the child's; the child's own grants still decide, and a name capNames does not map grants nothing. A cap is the host narrowing: it never asks the child for a grant of its own beyond its switch. The child answers with act.result: refused, or started and later finished. One request at a time per child.

act.result.idempotency: id is the actId, a dot and the phase.
act.result.description: Only from a child whose hello listed act: what became of act.request actId. phase refused with code (act_off: its switch is off; act_busy: it is running another; act_unavailable: it cannot run Work now; act_timeout: pickupBy has passed): nothing ran, and the proposal is accepted again on the host, not sent to this child again until it links again (act_busy: tried again later). phase started: it runs, shown on the child as a Work conversation the owner can stop there. phase finished with status, one of actStatuses (cancelled: stopped on the child, its switch was turned off, or act.cancel; timeout: it ran past maxRunMs), and summary, at most 160 characters of what the run said last: the proposal is done, failed or closed. What the run did comes up as an experience with started host and actId, and reaches her as her own Work does.

act.cancel.description: Only to a child whose hello listed act: stop act.request actId. code is why: act_cancelled (the owner dismissed the proposal on the site) or act_timeout (it ran past maxRunMs and a minute). The child stops the run and answers act.result finished cancelled, unless it was over already. Sent once, while the link is open; a child that misses it ends its run at maxRunMs.

call.offer.description: After welcome, on a link where both listed calls: what this child may be asked to do, [{name, version}] from calls, by is child. It says what the end can do, not what the owner allowed; it is said again after every welcome. An action the host does not know is left out by it.

call.granted.description: The answer to call.offer, and again whenever it changes: actions are the offered ones the owner approved for this device and that are granted now, [{name, version}]; providing are the host's own actions this child may call, [{name, version}]. An action in neither is not called. On every link the host sends call.granted before any call.ask, a resend of one from before included, and resends only asks of actions it grants then; a child holds an ask that comes before this link's call.granted, neither doing nor answering it. When the owner takes an action back, or the device is revoked, the host drops the asks of it it has never sent on any link and never sends them: they end as call_not_granted on the host. One sent on any link, acked or not, is not dropped: a long one it cancels (call.cancel, after this link's call.granted when it was sent on an earlier one), and whatever result comes is what happened, as for one that comes after its deadline.

call.ask.idempotency: id is the callId: made by the caller once, the same on every resend.
call.ask.description: Ask the other end to do action (calls) at version with args; callId is the frame's id, at most 57 characters so that its result's id (callId.result) fits limits.idPattern, for for ({kind, groupId?}: kind one of callAudiences, groupId only and always for group), answered by deadlineAt at the latest, milliseconds since the epoch (never seconds: at least 10^12, and at most 2^53 - 1) on the host's clock, whoever asks: the frame's at stays its sender's own clock, and a child converts by the offset from the serverTime of its latest welcome (taken anew on every link, a one-way trip's delay in it; a clock that drifts or jumps while a link lasts, which may be days, is not set right again until the next welcome, and the ends' deadlines are then that far apart). A caller gives at most callDeadlineMaxMs from when it asks to deadlineAt, longCallMaxMs for a long action (or one it does not know); a receiver holds an ask to that most from when it takes it, earlier than deadlineAt when deadlineAt is further, and does not refuse it for that (the core's call_deadline), so a caller that keeps to it and its receiver hold the same deadline, within the error of the child's clock offset. A resend carries the same deadlineAt, so an ask that comes after it is answered call_timeout and not done, and a long action still running then is stopped and answered call_timeout. The caller counts it call_timeout a minute after deadlineAt; a result that comes later is still what happened, and she is told it did after all, but no end does it again. The caller checks for first (calls); the receiver checks it again, and answers every ask with one call.result.

call.accepted.description: A long action's receiver has it, within callAcceptMs: call.progress and call.result follow.

call.progress.description: Where a long action is, the newest per callId counting (calls at once do not replace each other's): phase is a stage name of the action's own, never content (it matches limits.idPattern); waiting is owner while the receiver waits for the owner to answer on the device (at most ownerConfirmMaxMs).

call.event.description: The next piece of a streams action's result, sequence from 1, in order. Lost with the link: the result still comes whole in call.result, or the call ends unknown.

call.result.idempotency: id is the callId, a dot and result: callId.result.
call.result.description: What came of call.ask callId, at the action version it was done at (the ask's, or the one the receiver does when it answers version_unsupported). outcome done carries result, exactly the result fields of that version when this end knows it (calls names one version of each action; another passes, for the ends to read by what they know); failed carries error {code}, one of calls.failCodes; unknown carries neither: the receiver lost track midway, and no end does it again by itself. blobs are blobIds at transports.blobs, only for a blob action.

call.cancel.description: The caller no longer wants a long action callId: the receiver stops it and answers call.result failed with call_cancelled, or the result it already had.

link.versions.description: After welcome, on a link where both listed versions: contract is this end's schemaVersion, core {abi, commit} the shared core it runs: abi is what the other end judges by, commit the myriad-core commit this end was built from (40 hex digits; the native apps' CORE_PIN, the site's core/ pointer), only to show and to look into, app {name, version}, actions {name: version} of calls it knows. Each end sends it once per link.

link.verdict.description: The host's reading of the child's link.versions: usable is full, partial (stopped names what this link will not carry: frames, capabilities or actions the two do not read alike) or refused (the link closes with unsupported_protocol after it). Shown on the host's status and on the device.

stream.state.description: The newest value of something told as it changes, name and version from streams.state. Only on a link where both listed streams.

stream.event.idempotency: id is the event's own, made once by its sender.
stream.event.description: Something that happened, each one kept and acked, name and version from streams.event. Only on a link where both listed streams.

ack.description: Carries only the envelope's ack, for a child with nothing else to send. The host's frames always carry its ack, and it pings at least every heartbeat.

host.freeze.description: Only on the link of the device she lives on (its welcome said host app): she is frozen there for the move moveId (kind move: back to the site, the owner confirmed it; kind recover: another device takes her back from a daily backup). The device stops her parts (put aside, not destroyed), and for a move back says what it froze over HTTP and sends her; a device still on local-owner that has taken partner from its welcome moves first (welcome), and one that moves after it said what it froze says it again (the rows go by the new id). Said again after each welcome while it holds.

host.thaw.description: Only on the link of the device she lives on (its welcome said host app): the move moveId was called off; she goes on there as she was.

host.moved.description: Only on the link of a device that held her (its welcome said host app): she lives elsewhere now (holder site or a device id, at epoch). The link closes with host_moved next; the device writes its copy of her to a sealed file and lets it go.

error.description: A frame the host could not take, and the link stays up. ref is that frame's seq. Codes are in errorCodes; there is no message text. serverTime goes with clock_ahead only: the time the rows were compared with, in microseconds, real time when the server trusts its own clock (as the HTTPS clock_ahead answer).

fact.up.idempotency: id is made by the device once per batch, the same on every resend.
fact.up.description: Facts this device's senses gave, already through the host filter on this device (raw sensing never leaves it), up to her mind. facts is [{source, kind, at, until?, data}]: source and kind name the sense, at and until are milliseconds since the epoch, data is the filtered fact's fields. To a mind on the server they go in clear inside the TLS connection. To a mind on a PC they go through the server sealed (sealed, below), so the server relays what it cannot read; on the same 现场's LAN they go in clear over the direct connection. Facts only the PC itself senses (screen, windows, other agents' records) never travel; what of them its own gates let through to her goes up as a moment (agent.merope.screen and the other moments.kinds), never as facts.

hand.raise.description: Her mind wants to speak on the device the owner is using now (the front device). handId names this raise; tier is how far she wants to go (the arbiter's tier); exit is the way she would like (text, voice, notification); reason is a category, never content. expiresAt is milliseconds since the epoch: unanswered by then, it is dropped. Not kept or resent: after a reconnect the mind decides again from the facts in her log.

hand.answer.description: The front device's answer by its own hard bounds (do-not-disturb, a meeting, the place's bounds): it can only lower, never rewrite. allowed false names the bound that held. exit is the way it allows, at most the one asked.

hand.drop.description: She lets the raise go (the moment passed, or her mind moved).

say.line.idempotency: id is the line's id, the same on every resend.
say.line.description: Her words down to the front device, after hand.answer allowed them, or because the owner talked to her there. kind is one of sayKinds; perform is how she acts it. The device plays it, or keeps it until said or expired (timing.sayTtlMs).

say.delivered.idempotency: id is made by the device once, the same on every resend.
say.delivered.description: How much of a line was said aloud or shown, so her log holds what the owner actually heard.

lease.ask.description: A host core asks the server for her mind: why is talk (the owner spoke to her here), place (the owner's 现场 is here now) or force (the owner pressed 'come here'). epoch is the newest this core knows. The server queues asks, one at a time, and answers with lease.grant to the target and lease.epoch to everyone. An ask that does not move her now (the asker holds her already, the rules refuse it, or another holder has not given her up) is answered to the asker alone with lease.epoch for the grant that stands, so it knows where she still is.

lease.yield.idempotency: id is made by the holder once per yield.
lease.yield.description: The holder gives her mind up: going to sleep, the owner left its 现场, or the server asked. through is its last shared count (dseq) in each audience it wrote in, {audience: dseq}, an audience with none left out: the target catches up to them before it thinks. to is the core it gives her to, when it knows. Yielding is small on purpose, so it fits in the moment before a lid closes.

lease.grant.idempotency: id is the grant's epoch as text.
lease.grant.description: To the new holder: grant is {epoch, holder, issued, how, from?, through?, move?} as the log rules write it (log.fold reads the history); from is the holder it moved from (every grant but the first; grants kept from before it was written have none), whose rows through counts; through is per audience, as in lease.yield. A grant only goes to a holder: a freeze (how freeze, holder null, move naming the move) goes out as lease.epoch alone. The holder catches up to through in from's rows (lease.behind), then thinks. stopAfter is the server's stop time in microseconds (lease.here's stopAfter): how long the holder, cut off from the server and with the owner gone from its 现场, keeps thinking before it stops by itself. An interim host waits by the same value, so the holder runs lease.here with it; absent means three minutes. To an end whose hello listed deputy, the server counts a grant delivered only once lease.taken names it (an ack is of everything heard, a grant the end could not read too): until then the end may not know it holds her, and the server keeps the grant and sends it again after a reconnect. An end that did not list deputy: delivered once its ack covers it, as before.

lease.epoch.description: To every device: where her mind is now. A core that held an older epoch stops at once and becomes a child. While she moves house holder is null, how is freeze and move names the move: every side stops (lease.here says frozen) until a thaw or a commit, both issued by the server. To a holder that stopped by itself and is back in reach, a lease.epoch naming it at its epoch is the server saying the lease still stands: it drops lease.here's stoppedAt and thinks again. Devices show where she is from it. stopAfter as in lease.grant, so a holder that missed the grant still stops by the server's value. issued and from are the standing grant's (from absent when it has none), only to an end whose hello listed deputy (an older end's frame check refuses a field it does not take): with them a child holds the grant that stands whole, {epoch, holder, issued, how, from?, move?}, for lease.here to read with its deputy (a freeze checks only with its from).

lease.stopped.idempotency: id is made by the holder once per stop.
lease.stopped.description: Sent on reconnect by a holder that stopped by itself (cut off, and the owner gone from its 现场 for the self-stop time): when it stopped, so the server knows where the gap in her memory begins and ends.

lease.place.description: Where this device is and whether the owner is with it: place is the device's own opaque token for the 现场 it is in (never a name, an address or a network's name; the same 现场 gives the same token on every device of the owner's, how is the devices' business), absent when it does not know; ownerHere is whether the owner is using this device now. Sent when either changes, and after welcome. The holder of the lease sends it too. The server keeps the latest of each device: a takeover needs the holder's place and a fresher sighting of the owner in another one (lease.takeover).

lease.takeover.description: To a holder coming back after the server took her over: grant is the takeover, through the last of its rows the server had in each audience, {audience: dseq} (an audience left out: none).
