It becomes a child and sends its rows past through, which are her own memory catching up, not another her.

lease.deputy.idempotency: id is made by the server once per deputy, the same on every resend.
lease.deputy.description: Only to an end whose hello listed deputy, that can host her and keeps up with her log (the owner's private talk and her own audience not behind): the server's leave, issued ahead of time, to be her interim host while the holder is out of its reach. deputy is {holder, under, issued, until, order} as the log rules write it (lease.here reads it): holder is this end (a clock node), under the epoch standing when it was issued, which the end writes her rows at while interim, issued the server's clock then, until when it runs out in microseconds (at most timing.deputyMaxMs after issued), order where the server put this end among those it gave deputies to, from 1, the one the owner used last (shown; nothing decides by it yet). The server issues a new one each time the end links and every hour after, and again whenever it issues a grant; it keeps every one it issued and marks rows by those alone, so a deputy it did not issue proves nothing. The end keeps the newest and observes issued into its clock. lease.here (given the grant that stands, whole from lease.epoch's issued, and a now as its rows' clock reads, never behind real time) says interim while the holder has been out of its reach for the stop time, the owner is with it, and the deputy is for the epoch that stands and has not run out: she thinks there, knowing she is interim and may be thinking elsewhere too; back in reach, or the deputy run out, she stops there and its rows go up as ever, kept and marked concurrent. The server keeps it until lease.taken names it.

lease.taken.description: From an end whose hello listed deputy: it has read the lease.grant or lease.deputy (of names which) with this id through and keeps it. The server counts that frame delivered only on this, never on an ack: the ack is of everything heard, a frame the end refused too. Sent again whenever that frame comes again, a duplicate id too (unlike other reliable frames, which a duplicate only acks): the server sends it again because it did not hear this. One the end could not read is not answered, and the server keeps it.

log.vector.description: What this core holds of one audience's log: vector is {origin: last dseq held without gaps}, beyond what it holds past a gap (log.holdings). Sent after welcome for each audience it keeps, after merging what it downloaded by a log.full link, and in answer to one; the other side then sends what is missing with log.rows. ask lists rows this core holds whose bodies did not come or came spoilt (nodes.wire_take ask), each at most once per link session: the other side sends them again with their bodies after what is missing (nodes.wire_send ask). On a link where both listed log.pages, what is missing goes a page at a time (log.rows more). Once this core has settled the batch that carries more (merged it, or refused it with an error answer such as clock_ahead), it sends log.vector again with after set to it, and only then; one sent for any other reason has no after. The other side answers a log.vector with a page of at most limits.logPageBatches batches in all: first what the vector and beyond show missing, then the rows asked again for (the ones left from its previous page first, then this log.vector's own ask; at most maxItems.ask of them, the rest kept for the page after). While a page it sent is unfinished, that is, its more not yet named by an after, only a log.vector whose after names that page gets the next one, and any other gets no rows: a duplicate or stale log.vector never sends rows again, and an end has at most one unfinished page of an audience on a link. A log.vector naming the unfinished page whose vector and beyond are those of the one that asked for it, when that page carried rows the vector lacked, made no headway (its rows were refused): that page is finished and no page follows it; the next log.vector without after is answered with a page again. A page of only rows asked again for leaves the vector as it was and is headway all the same. Paging starts over on every link, and a page id is never used again on another link, so a batch sent again after a reconnect names no page of the new one. Where a page ends is said only by more: the log.vector an end sends of its own after a round of batches (its vector, for the other side to send what it lacks) is not the end of a page; without log.pages it is the only sign that a round is over.

log.rows.idempotency: id is made by the sender once per batch.
log.rows.description: A batch of one audience's rows (log.answer: every forget first). rows are row envelopes; payloads is [{ref, data}] for the payloads the rows point at, data base64, sealed per object when S5 lands. Rows only a PC keeps that travel between PCs go sealed to the receiving PC. The receiver checks the batch (log.admit) and merges it (log.merge); a batch with a clock too far ahead is refused whole with error clock_ahead and the server's time. withheld is [{id, why}] for the rows here that point at a payload and go without it (nodes.wire_send): a why other than no_body or bad_body is for good, and the receiver does not ask for it again. more is only on a link where both listed log.pages, on the last batch of a page when more is to go (nodes.wire_send more): an id the sender makes once per page and never on another link (limits.idPattern), which the receiver names as after in the log.vector it sends once it has settled that batch. The last batch of the last page carries no more; to an end that did not list log.pages every batch goes at once, as before, and none carries more. A log page in a file never carries more.

log.full.description: For a new host core's first full sync: where to download the audience's log over HTTPS (url, a single-use link valid until expiresAt), and the vector it holds. Sent only to a link whose hello listed log.full; to one that did not, the server sends the same rows over the link in log.rows batches. Increments then go over the link.

peer.publish.idempotency: id is made by the device once per key pair.
peer.publish.description: This device's public keys, base64: signKey (Ed25519) proves it on the LAN; sealKey (X25519) is what others seal to. Made on the device; the private halves never leave it. The server shows them to the owner, who confirms the device once (pairing); only then do other devices get them.

peer.keys.description: The owner's paired devices: [{deviceId, name, signKey, sealKey, keyId}]. keyId is the first 16 bytes of sha256 of sealKey's bytes, in hex. A device not in it is not one of hers: refused on the LAN, never sealed to.

peer.hello.description: LAN only, the dialer's first frame: who it says it is and 32 random bytes (base64). partner is the id it goes by (its holder's owner: a partner id, or local-owner until it has moved): the listener passes it as peer to nodes.wire_take and log.admit, and answers with nodes.wire_send and log.answer only when it is the listener's own id (partner::exchange). Devices under two ids exchange no rows.

peer.welcome.description: LAN only, the listener's answer: who it is, its own nonce, the sha256 of its TLS certificate (hex), and proof: its Ed25519 signature (base64) over the canonical JSON {dialer, dialerNonce, listener, listenerNonce, certHash, purpose: 'myriad-link-lan/2 listener'}. The dialer checks it against peer.keys and that certHash is the certificate it is talking to. partner is the listener's id, as in peer.hello: the dialer passes it as peer, and exchanges rows only when it is its own id.

peer.proof.description: LAN only, the dialer's proof: its signature over the same object with purpose 'myriad-link-lan/2 dialer'. Only then do other frames flow; anything else first closes with peer_proof_failed.

group.lend.idempotency: id is made by the server once per lend; a lend is never sent again (delivery reliable only for its id and its ack), so the mind takes each id once.
group.lend.description: To the core her mind is on, when that is a PC: new messages in a group she is in, lent for her to think with. group is the group's audience (group:<id>), name what the group is called there. messages are the new ones and recent the ones just before them, oldest first, each {id, from, name, text, at, toHer?, who?}: id the platform's message id as text, from the member's id in the group's audience (the subject its rows use), name what the member is called there, at milliseconds since the epoch, toHer whether it was addressed to her (a mention or a reply to her), who who wrote it as the server knows them, in the shape of the group mind's identified answer: {kind: member, user_id, bound} for someone paired with an account on the site (bound: their binding there is current), {kind: stranger} for anyone else; the community has no guests, so only a paired account makes a member. who absent: the server could not tell (the mind takes it as unknown). owner is the site owner's user id, the identified answer's owner: who hosts her in the group (a stranger's reply is on their account). So her mind on a PC knows the group's people as the server does. through is the highest dseq of this PC's rows the server holds in the group's audience, past any gap too (absent: none), so the rows the mind writes there never use a number twice: the PC keeps none of that audience on disk, and a count kept only in memory is gone after a restart. The mind numbers past the larger of through and the highest it sent there since it started, and writes rows in an audience it does not hold only for a lend it took since it started; a number skipped is harmless, one used twice is refused. What she knows of the group (her own lines there, what she noted of its members) is the group's log, which the mind reads with log.vector as the holder. The PC keeps none of it on disk and lets it go when she is done or the lease moves; only the server keeps a group. Sent only while that PC holds the lease and only on a link whose hello listed lend, once per lend: a lend is the mind's once the PC's ack covers it (whether she says anything is hers), and one not acked when the lease moves or the link closes is the server's again (its lines go to the server's group mind).

group.say.idempotency: id is made by the mind once per line, the same on every resend.
group.say.description: Her mind on a PC says text in a group: the server sends it there as her, the way it sends her own lines. replyTo is the message id she answers, lend the group.lend it comes from. Her line and what she noted are hers to write: the mind writes them as rows of the group's audience at its epoch and sends them with log.rows, and the server keeps them; the PC keeps neither on disk (it writes them for the server, then lets them go). Taken only from the holder: from a core that does not hold the lease it is refused by the frame check as a frame from a role it does not have (error bad_frame, with ref); answered with group.said.

group.said.description: The answer to group.say: sayId is its id, sent whether the line went out. code, when it did not, is why: group_unknown (a group the server does not keep or did not lend), or unavailable when the platform would not take it or the text is empty; the mind does not say it again on its own.

chat.lend.idempotency: id is made by the server once per lend; a lend is never sent again (delivery reliable only for its id and its ack), so the mind takes each id once.
chat.lend.description: To the core her mind is on, when that is a PC: new messages someone sent her in a private chat on a chat app the server reaches (a bot), lent for her to think with, as group.lend lends a group's. chat is that talk's audience (personal:<id>, id the one she talks with as her log names them), name what they are called there, who who they are as the server knows them, in group.lend's shape ({kind: member, user_id, bound}: a private chat is lent only with someone paired with an account on the site). messages are the new ones and recent the ones just before them, oldest first, each {id, text, at, mine?}: id the platform's message id as text, at milliseconds since the epoch, mine true for a line she said there (recent only). When the one she talks with is not the partner (chat is not the PC's own holder's personal audience), it is talk the PC does not hold: it keeps none of it on disk and lets it go when she is done or the lease moves, and what she knows of them is that audience's log, which the mind reads with log.vector as the holder; only the server keeps it. When it is the partner, it is the partner's own talk, which the PC holds and keeps as it keeps that talk's rows. through is as in group.lend, for chat's audience, and is sent only when the PC does not hold it. Sent only while that PC holds the lease and only on a link whose hello listed lend, once per lend: a lend is the mind's once the PC's ack covers it (whether she says anything is hers), and one not acked when the lease moves or the link closes is the server's again (the message is held for when she is back).

chat.say.idempotency: id is made by the mind once per line, the same on every resend.
chat.say.description: Her mind on a PC says text in a private chat: the server sends it there as her, the way it sends her own lines. replyTo is the message id she answers, lend the chat.lend it comes from. Her line and what she noted are hers to write: the mind writes them as rows of the chat's audience at its epoch and sends them with log.rows, and the server keeps them; when the one she talks with is not the partner, the PC keeps neither on disk (it writes them for the server, then lets them go). Taken only from the holder: from a core that does not hold the lease it is refused by the frame check as a frame from a role it does not have (error bad_frame, with ref); answered with chat.said.

chat.said.description: The answer to chat.say: sayId is its id, sent whether the line went out. code, when it did not, is why: chat_unknown (a chat the server does not keep or did not lend), or unavailable when the platform would not take it or the text is empty; the mind does not say it again on its own.

errorCodes.unknown_frame: A frame type this end does not know (a newer end): ignored.
errorCodes.bad_frame: Not an envelope, a body without its required fields or with fields it does not take, both or neither of a oneOf pair, or a frame from a role the sender does not have (a mind frame from a core that does not hold the lease).
errorCodes.not_ready: A frame other than hello before hello: ignored; the host still waits for hello.
errorCodes.binary_unsupported: A binary frame: the link has none (encoding.text).
errorCodes.input_too_long: input text is longer than limits.maxTextChars.
errorCodes.bad_id: An id or turnId that does not match limits.idPattern.
errorCodes.surface_unsupported: A surface this host does not take input from.
errorCodes.turn_unknown: run.resume for a turn the host does not have.
errorCodes.agent_access_denied: The site owner may not use the agent now.
errorCodes.host_frozen: run.rejected: she is moving between her ends; nothing reaches her until the move is done or cancelled.
errorCodes.host_moved: run.rejected: she does not live on this site now.
errorCodes.mind_elsewhere: run.rejected: she is not thinking here now: her mind is on another of your devices, or was just handed back and the site is still catching up on what that device wrote. The turn did not reach her; the child shows the owner it was not sent.
errorCodes.internal_error: Something failed on the host; trying again later may work.
errorCodes.not_this_device: A runId that is not one this device's turns started.
errorCodes.too_large: Over limits.maxFrameBytes, or a field longer than its limit (playback.observe: upcomingText 7200 bytes, rig 16 KiB; work.recall: query limits.maxTextChars characters).
errorCodes.outfit_unknown: outfit.wear named a set that is not in her wardrobe, or has no rig.
errorCodes.proposal_unknown: proposal.answer named a proposal that is not open: answered already, expired, or not hers to the site owner.
errorCodes.place_unknown: proposal.answer asked to run a proposal where it cannot run: not one of the card's places.
errorCodes.card_unknown: card.answer named a card that is not one of the owner's, or a version it never had.
errorCodes.card_closed: card.answer answered a version of a card that asks nothing: no action but open.
errorCodes.card_action_unknown: card.answer named an action that version does not have, or open.
errorCodes.card_stale: card.answered kept an answer to a version that is not the latest: the answer stands for what the owner saw, and the latest still waits on them.
errorCodes.act_off: act.result: the child's switch for the site asking it to act is off.
errorCodes.act_busy: act.result: the child is running another of the host's requests.
errorCodes.act_unavailable: act.result: the child cannot run Work now (it is not set up, or none of its tools may be used). Also why the host cannot send a request: no child that takes act is linked.
errorCodes.act_timeout: An act.request not started by pickupBy, or a run past maxRunMs.
errorCodes.act_cancelled: act.cancel: the owner dismissed the proposal on the site.
errorCodes.act_revoked: The child was removed from the site, or the site has another owner, while its request was open: the proposal failed.
errorCodes.version_unsupported: An envelope v this end does not read, or (call.result) an action version the receiver does not do.
errorCodes.too_many: An array over the frame's maxItems.
errorCodes.bad_sealed: A sealed field not of the sealing shape, or of another suite.
errorCodes.not_for_me: Sealed to another device: relay it, do not open it.
errorCodes.not_holder: A lease frame from a core that does not hold the epoch it names.
errorCodes.stale_epoch: A lease frame for an epoch that no longer stands.
errorCodes.group_unknown: A group frame naming a group the server does not keep, one she is not in, or one the server did not lend that core.
errorCodes.chat_unknown: A chat frame naming a private chat the server does not keep, one no chat app reaches now, or one the server did not lend that core.
errorCodes.clock_ahead: log.rows refused whole: a row's clock more than five minutes ahead. Carries serverTime; the sender measures its offset, repairs its unsynced rows and sends again.
errorCodes.sync_off: A frame of a sync family (sync.families) on a link whose welcome said sync off.
errorCodes.call_unknown: call.result: the receiver does not offer this action (not in its call.offer, or not in calls).
errorCodes.call_not_granted: call.result: the owner did not approve this action's group for this end, or it is not granted now (the receiver's own grants do not allow it).
errorCodes.call_unavailable: call.result: the end the call is for is not linked now; the host answers at once and queues nothing.
errorCodes.wrong_audience: call.result: the action may not be called for this for: a private action outside the owner's private talk, any action for someone else's private talk (other), a group action for another group.
errorCodes.declined: call.result: the owner, asked on the device, said no, or did not answer within ownerConfirmMaxMs.
errorCodes.not_now: call.result: the receiver's do-not-disturb or bounds hold it back now; asking later may work.

revoked.description: The device was removed from the site, or gave its token back.

owner_changed.description: The site has another owner; this device was the old owner's.

replaced.description: Another connection of this same device took over.

host_moved.description: Her lease moved her to another end, or the end she lived on was removed. To a device that was welcomed as the one she lives on (host app) and does not hold her at the hostEpoch it says any more: she moved, and it lets its copy go. To any other child the upgrade is refused with host_moved, naming where she lives; it reconnects seldom.

host_frozen.description: She is moving: her host lease is frozen and no end has her. The upgrade is refused with host_frozen until the move is done or cancelled; a child keeps reconnecting with backoff and says she is moving.

bad_frame.description: The hello could not be taken: not an envelope, a body without what it needs, or a role or surface this host does not know.

unsupported_protocol.description: hello.protocol is not this host's (protocol). Every end speaks one protocol; neither falls back. An end closed with it after saying hello in its own protocol tells the owner the site is to be updated; the site, closing an end whose hello said another, shows on its devices page that the app on that device is to be updated. Both say it by the code, never with the reason's text.

timeout.description: No hello in time, or nothing heard for missedHeartbeats heartbeats.

unavailable.description: The host is stopping or cannot serve the link now.

peer_unknown.description: LAN: the device is not one of the owner's paired devices (peer.keys).

peer_proof_failed.description: LAN: a proof that does not verify, a certificate hash that is not this connection's, or a frame before the proofs.

epoch_stale.description: A core that dialled as her mind holds an epoch that no longer stands: it stops thinking and reconnects as a child.

version_unsupported.description: The envelope's v is not one this end reads.
